h: The Three Camps and the Holiness of Human Service

p: נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן גַּם הֵם
"Take a census of the sons of Gershon, they too"
In the holy Zohar at the beginning of this parsha:
אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם לֹא יַחְשׁוֹב ה׳ לוֹ עָוֹן
"Fortunate is the man to whom Hashem does not reckon iniquity,
and in whose spirit there is no deceit" (Tehillim 32:2).
its beginning is not its end,
and its end is not its beginning.
Meaning: the sense of the pasuk,
"to whom Hashem does not reckon iniquity,"
רַק ה׳ לֹא יַחְשׁוֹב לוֹ לְעָוֹן
only Hashem does not reckon it to him as iniquity;
while the end of the pasuk,
"and in whose spirit there is no deceit,"
implies that there is none in him at all.
to whom Hashem does not reckon iniquity'
When there is no deceit in his spirit."
how this answers the difficulty of the pasuk's contradiction;
and also what connection this opening has
לְפָרָשָׁה נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן
to the parsha "Take a census of the sons of Gershon."
But the order of the parshiyos
from the beginning of Sefer Bamidbar is:
שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ כָּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
"Take a census of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael" etc.,
and their number in general, in particular, and by banners.
and the expression "naso" is not said there.
נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי קְהָת וְגוֹ׳
"Take a census of the sons of Kehas" etc.,
נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן גַּם הֵם
"Take a census of the sons of Gershon, they too";
and afterward, "the sons of Merari according to their families,"
and "naso" is not written with them.
the parsha of sending out from the camps.
וַיְהִי בְּיוֹם כַּלּוֹת מֹשֶׁה (בְּמִדְבַּר ז, א)
"And it was on the day Moshe finished" (Bamidbar 7:1),
where the camp of the Shechinah was formed,
the camp of Yisrael and the camp of the Levi'im.
And therefore it is written first,
שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ כָּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"Take a census of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael";
that is, that there should be in them
the holiness of the camps of Yisrael.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא ד)
in the manner of what is written in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 4):
"Therefore He gave them a raised head
וְאָמַר לוֹ כִּי תִשָּׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ
and said to him, 'When you take the census (lift the head).'"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּמִסְפַּר הַלְוִיִּם מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ
And afterward, in the count of the Levi'im from one month old,
for the main elevation of the Levi'im
is only from when they came to the age of service.
For the holiness of the camp of Yisrael
is that they are occupied with the matters of this world,
but they fix times for Torah
And even in the matters of the business of this world,
כְּשֶׁעוֹסֵק בָּהֶם עִם כַּוָּנָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
when one engages in them with intent for the sake of Heaven,
so that he can fix times for Torah
and raise their children to Torah study,
as the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote
עַל מַאֲמַר וְכָל מַעֲשֶׂיךָ יִהְיוּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
on the saying "And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven"
שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה עִנְיְנֵי הַגּוּף לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
that when a person does bodily matters for the sake of Heaven,
all of it becomes the performance of mitzvos;
גַּם עֵסֶק סְתָם מִצְוֹת וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
also occupation with ordinary mitzvos and acts of kindness,
And this is the holiness of the camp of Yisrael.
And the holiness of the camp of the Levi'im
הוּא שֶׁהֵם פְּנוּיִים רַק לַתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה
is that they are free only for Torah and avodah,
for they have no portion in the Land,
only Hashem is their portion and inheritance,
וְאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם עֵסֶק מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and they have no occupation at all with matters of this world,
רַק כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה כַּוָּנַת בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם
only as was the purpose of man's creation,
"And I was created to serve my Maker."
from when they entered the age of service,
from thirty years old and upward.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי בְּמִסְפַּר הַלְוִיִּם מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ
And therefore in the count of the Levi'im from one month old
and "naso" is not written with them;
and afterward, in the count of the Levi'im
from thirty years old and upward,
כְּתִיב נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי קְהָת
it is written, "Take a census of the sons of Kehas."
And it is stated (Bamidbar Rabbah, beginning of this parsha, 6:1):
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגֵּרְשׁוֹן בְּכוֹר כּוּלֵּי
the pasuk placed him before Gershon, etc.:
than the firstborn who came out first," etc.
And afterward it is stated in the Midrash there:
"Because Kehas was among those who carried the Aron,
the pasuk placed Kehas first," etc.
That is, the Aron was holy of holies,
as it is written, "And Aharon was set apart
to sanctify him as holy of holies" etc.
and this is called the camp of the Shechinah;
and the sons of Kehas carried the Aron,
and therefore it placed him before Gershon.
וּבִבְנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן לְשׁוֹן נָשֹׂא
And with the sons of Gershon too the expression "naso" is written,
that the sons of Gershon too are like them,
And as for why with the sons of Merari
that even within the holiness of the Levi'im,
שֶׁהוּא מִי שֶׁהוּא פָּנוּי רַק לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנוֹ
which is one who is free only to serve his Maker,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט, ב)
אִם לַעֲמַל פֶּה אִם לַעֲמַל מְלָאכָה
whether for toil of the mouth or toil of work;
you must say he was created for toil of the mouth;
and I still do not know
אִם לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה אִם לַעֲמַל שִׂיחָה
whether for toil of Torah or toil of conversation;
כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא יָמוּשׁ וְגוֹ׳ (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ א, ח)
when it says, 'It shall not depart' etc. (Yehoshua 1:8),
you must say he was created for toil of Torah."
that certainly "toil of work" does not mean
שֶׁעַל זֶה לֹא יִתָּכֵן לוֹמַר סָפֵק
for about that one could not say there is a doubt
for the toil of bodily work.
certainly does not mean idle talk,
for about that there is no doubt
that it is not the purpose of man's creation.
שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הָאָדָם נִבְרָא לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנוֹ
that certainly man was created to serve his Maker;
is in the manner of the work of the Mishkan,
which is the performance of mitzvos,
and it says that the goal is toil of the mouth,
כָּל עֲמַל אָדָם לְפִיהוּ (קֹהֶלֶת ו, ז)
"All the toil of a man is for his mouth" (Koheles 6:7),
and "his mouth" is written without specification.
similar to what Rabbi Yochanan said,
וּלְוַאי שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם כָּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
"If only a person would pray the entire day"
"When it says, 'It shall not depart' etc.,
you must say he was created for toil of Torah."
That is, the main goal is toil of Torah;
for one whose Torah is his occupation,
for he would review his learning every thirty days
וְכֵן מִצְוַת שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
and likewise a mitzvah that can be done by others
is set aside for Torah study
toil of conversation, which is prayer,
and toil of work, which is the practical mitzvos,

p: the holiness of the camp of Yisrael
is those who engage in bodily matters
only with intent for the sake of Heaven,
and who fix times for Torah.
And the holiness of the camp of the Levi'im
הוּא שֶׁהֵם פְּנוּיִם רַק לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנוֹ
is that they are free only to serve their Maker;
and in this there are the three levels mentioned:
the sons of Kehas correspond to toil of Torah,
and the Aron is the words of Torah,
וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו גַּם כֵּן קוֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים
and Aharon and his sons are also holy of holies,
for they are the words of Torah itself,
"For the lips of the Kohen shall guard knowledge,
and they shall seek Torah from his mouth";
and this is the camp of the Shechinah.
And the sons of Kehas, who carry the Aron,
and this is the first level,
as written, "he was created for toil of Torah";
and therefore the pasuk placed him first.
וּבְנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן הֵם כְּנֶגֶד עֲמַל שִׂיחָה
And the sons of Gershon correspond to toil of conversation,
for they carried the curtains of the Mishkan
And the Mishkan is named mainly for the curtains,
"And you shall make a covering for the tent" (Shemos 26:14);
וּכְתִיב כִּי בֵיתִי בֵּית תְּפִלָּה וְגוֹ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, ז)
and it is written, "For My house shall be called a house of prayer" etc. (Yeshayahu 56:7);
and the Mishkan is called a house of prayer.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי כְּתִיב גַּם בִּבְנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן
And therefore it is written with the sons of Gershon too
שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן יֵשׁ לָהֶם מַעֲלָה
for they too have a high level
וּלְוַאי שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם כָּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
"If only a person would pray the entire day."
And afterward the sons of Merari,
the work of the Mishkan and the work of the mitzvos;
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי לֹא כְּתִיב בָּהֶם לְשׁוֹן נָשֹׂא
and therefore the expression "naso" is not written with them,
since it is the last and lowest level
of the levels of the camp of the Levi'im,
שֶׁהוּא פָּנוּי רַק לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנוֹ
that one is free only to serve his Maker.
And even in the camp of Yisrael there is holiness,
שֶׁעֲסוּקִין גַּם כֵּן בְּמִצְוֹת וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
for they too are occupied with mitzvos and acts of kindness,
and likewise occupation with intent for the sake of Heaven,
which also becomes a matter of mitzvah.

p: the parsha of sending away the impure:
the metzora is sent outside all three camps,
for this corresponds to jealousy and anger,
which have no share at all in Yisrael.
And the zav, who corresponds to the kelipah of desire,
is sent outside the camp of the Levi'im;
for one who is free for Torah and avodah,
יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ לְחַבֵּל הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה
has the power to destroy the inclination of desire
And one impure through the dead is sent
only outside the camp of the Shechinah,
and one who holds fast to words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת (תַּעֲנִית ה, ב)
as written, "Yaakov Avinu did not die" (Taanis 5b),
and this has been explained elsewhere.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי פָּתַח הַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בִּפְתִיחָה זוֹ
And therefore the holy Zohar opened with this opening:
for it is written in the parsha
that there is the holiness of the camp of Yisrael
and of the camp of the Levi'im;
yet "there is no righteous man on earth
אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ)
who does good and does not sin" (Koheles 7:20);
אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם לֹא יַחְשׁוֹב ה׳ לוֹ עָוֹן
"Fortunate is the man to whom Hashem does not reckon iniquity."
That is, Hashem Yisbarach gave us
as it is written, "And the goat shall bear upon itself
and they expounded in the Midrash Rabbah (Toldos, Bereishis Rabbah 65:15):
"'And the goat shall bear' — this is Esav;
that is, Hashem Yisbarach makes clear
to do the will of our Father in Heaven,
The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms,"
found in the nations of the world,
the leaven in the dough enters the heart of Yisrael.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לֹא יַחְשׁוֹב ה׳ לוֹ עָוֹן
And this is what it says, "Hashem does not reckon iniquity to him":
שֶׁאֵין הֶעָוֹן נֶחְשָׁב בַּחֶשְׁבּוֹן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
for the iniquity is not counted against Yisrael,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר זֶה עֵשָׂו וְכוּלֵּי
as written, "'And the goat shall bear' — this is Esav," etc.
When there is no deceit in his spirit":
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין בְּרוּחַ הַחַיִּים שֶׁלּוֹ רְמִיָּה
that is, there is no deceit in his spirit of life,
for that is the portion of Esav.
And this follows what they said
are the leaven in the dough, etc.,
הוּא מַה שֶּׁקִּיבֵּל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
is what Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, accepted,
not to mix the Erev Rav among them,
as written in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah 42:6, Ki Sisa):
only because they saw the greatness of Yisrael,
"Converts are not accepted in the days of Mashiach;
לֹא קִבְּלוּ גֵּרִים לֹא בִּימֵי דָוִד
they did not accept converts in the days of David
nor in the days of Shlomo."
after the fact they are converts
is the leaven in the dough,
and from them Hashem Yisbarach will make a clarification
and separate them from Yisrael entirely,
and they will leave the holiness of the camp of Yisrael;
that there will be found among them
one who intended for the sake of Heaven,
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar:
"When? When there is no deceit in his spirit"
that he is not one of that Erev Rav
who are truly the leaven in the dough;
כִּי רְמִיָּה הוּא חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו
for deceit is the portion of Esav,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (תּוֹלְדוֹת פָּרָשָׁה סג)
"Here is the worthless thing I created in My world";
and his portion was "for game was in his mouth,"
And he told him, "In the house of study":
And even regarding the future it is stated (Tanchuma, Tzav 2):
He wraps himself in his tallis like an elder
that is, he wishes to deceive
בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And only about this it says,
"And if your nest be set among the stars"
מִשָּׁם אוֹרִידְךָ נְאוּם ה׳ (עוֹבַדְיָה א, ד)
"from there I will bring you down, says Hashem" (Ovadiah 1:4).
When there is no deceit in his spirit"
that he is not of that Erev Rav.
וְזֶהוּ שַׁיָּיכוּת פְּתִיחַת הַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ לְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ
And this is the connection of the holy Zohar's opening to this parsha.
And according to this is resolved
in the contradiction of the pasuk, as stated.

p: the holiness of all three camps.
That is, in the three Shabbos meals:
at the meal of Erev Shabbos night,
which is yirah and in which yirah rests
(in the holy Zohar, in the Introduction),
a person merits the holiness of the camp of Yisrael;
becomes one of "those who fear My Name,"
and the awe of Shabbos is upon even the am ha'aretz;
and at the meal of the Field of Apples he merits
when on weekdays it is the time when
יֵצֵא אָדָם לְפׇעֳלוֹ וְלַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ עֲדֵי עָרֶב (תְּהִלִּים קד, כג)
"man goes out to his work and to his labor until evening" (Tehillim 104:23),
and the Jew leaves all his affairs
for the honor of Hashem Yisbarach,
each in whatever he is occupied with,
they then merit the holiness of the camp of the Levi'im,
שֶׁהֵם פְּנוּיִם רַק לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנוֹ
who are free only to serve their Maker.
which is the meal of Ze'ir Anpin,
the aspect of the Name Havayah,
they then merit the holiness of the camp of the Shechinah.
And likewise they merit the three levels
within the camp of the Levi'im that we mentioned:
the level of toil of Torah,
for on Shabbos it should be made entirely Torah
frees himself for words of Torah;
which is the performance of mitzvos:
although on Shabbos there are no positive mitzvos,
but its mitzvah is in passive restraint,
except for Kiddush of the day and oneg Shabbos;
"If one sat and did not commit a transgression,
he is given reward like one who performs a mitzvah";
and on Shabbos it is considered
that a matter of transgression came his way
and he was saved from it,
all the weekdays to activity and labor,
such as sorting and the like;
and when he sits and refrains from it,
he is considered as performing a mitzvah all day,
and this is toil of work and the performance of mitzvos.
And toil of conversation, which is prayer,
גַּם כֵּן זוֹכֶה כָּל אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת
each one also merits on Shabbos;
for each one is called "My house of prayer,"
and as written in the Tikkunim and the holy Zohar
עַל פִּי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת לְדוֹרֹתָם
on "to make the Shabbos throughout their generations":
דְּעָבִיד לוֹן דִּירָה בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא
that one makes them a dwelling in the two chambers of the heart;
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת שׁוֹכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל
for on Shabbos Hashem Yisbarach dwells in the heart of Yisrael,
and all Yisrael are called "My house of prayer."
And likewise we say at Minchah of Shabbos,
וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי לְךָ ה׳ עֵת רָצוֹן
"And as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, at a time of favor";
and on Shabbos a person merits
the holiness of all the camps, as stated.
